editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (787 words, within the 400-1200 range). Clear Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis flow, appropriate technical depth on the 7060XE7 portfolio, and honest limitations section on pricing and adoption.
editor_notes.source_verification: All three source snapshots fetched at HTTP 200 and read from disk. source-0.html.gz (Arista press release, arista.com): CONFIRMED the core facts — 'SANTA CLARA, Calif. - June 9, 2026' launch date; 7060XE7 Series as a 1.6T portfolio; model lineup (7060XE7-64PS/64PRS air-cooled 4RU 64x1.6T Q4'26; 7060XE7-64PRS-RV3-L liquid-cooled 224G SerDes no internal fans Q1'27; 7060XE7-128PE air-cooled 4RU 128x800G 100G SerDes Q1'27); EOS + DLB/CLB/MRC/LLR software; and all five quotes VERBATIM (Lamoreaux, Borkar/Azure Maia+Fairwater, Nagarajan/Meta, Thiagarajan/Oracle RDMA, Khamisy/Broadcom Tomahawk 6 102-Tbps). Note: the PR describes the liquid-cooled unit as '2OU' (ORv3 Open Rack Unit), while the article says '2RU'. source-1.html.gz (Network World): CONFIRMED 'built on Broadcom Tomahawk 6 silicon', AMD collaboration on next-gen compute silicon and NICs for scale-out fabrics, and full OCP support for MRC steering around congestion. source-2.html.gz (SDxCentral): CONFIRMED 'growing cohort of vendors offering 1.6 Tb/s (1.6T) networking switches, targeting AI-centric network architectures' and the trio-of-switches framing. However, two claims explicitly attributed to SDxCentral are NOT in the SDxCentral snapshot: (a) 'AI clusters expanding from thousands to hundreds of thousands of accelerators' — this phrasing actually comes from the Arista PR ('As AI workloads scale from thousands to hundreds of thousands of XPUs'); (b) 'Ethernet is expanding into scale-up networking, the domain long dominated by Nvidia's NVLink' — 'scale-up' appears in the Arista PR and Network World but NOT in SDxCentral, and 'NVLink' appears in none of the three cited sources.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Headline, summary, and Overview lead are fully sourced and accurate (7060XE7, 1.6T, Broadcom Tomahawk 6, rack-scale AI fabrics, June 9 launch, Microsoft/Meta/Oracle backing). Product specs and all direct quotes verified verbatim. The only issues are two misattributions to SDxCentral (both underlying facts are true and supported by the Arista PR / Network World, so this is a wrong-outlet citation problem, not a fabricated event), one unsupported analytical characterization ('NVLink' not in any cited source), and a '2RU' vs '2OU' form-factor imprecision. All confined to subordinate context/analysis, not the headline/summary/lead.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional. No sensationalism, no AI self-reference. Appropriate hedging in the 'What We Don't Know' section.
editor_notes.originality: New topic. No existing article covers the Arista 7060XE7 or its Tomahawk 6 launch. Related prior coverage (Nvidia Spectrum-X revenue lead 2026-07-01, Upscale AI/UALink 2026-07-02, Cisco Silicon One G300) is referenced as context, not duplicated.
concerns: Two claims attributed to SDxCentral do not appear in the SDxCentral article: the 'thousands to hundreds of thousands of accelerators' scaling figure (which is actually from the Arista press release) and the 'Ethernet expanding into scale-up networking, the domain long dominated by Nvidia's NVLink' framing (scale-up is supported by Arista/Network World; NVLink is in no cited source).
The 7060XE7-64PRS-RV3-L is described as a '2RU' switch; the Arista press release specifies a '2OU' (ORv3 Open Rack Unit) form factor.
recommendations: File a corrections record documenting the two SDxCentral misattributions and the 2OU/2RU form-factor imprecision so readers see the accurate attribution.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS. The article's central event and all specifics/quotes in the headline, summary, and lead are solidly sourced and verbatim-accurate. The recoverable issues are two wrong-outlet attributions (facts true and sourced elsewhere), one unsupported NVLink characterization in the Analysis section, and a minor 2OU/2RU form-factor slip — all in subordinate positions, each honestly summarizable in a corrections note. None gut the lead or constitute a pattern of invented events, so REJECT is not warranted.
